text:
zoe: Heads up — main dashboard charts are noticeably slower post-canary. Heatmap LCP up ~600ms on EU canary.

miguel: saw that in perf dashboard, interesting. Only happened after telemetry sidecar roll

sara: build artifact comparison:
```
main.js 5.2MB -> 7.0MB (+1.8MB)
vendors.js unchanged
```
looks like telemetry bundles got inlined instead of lazy load

aleks: I think the prefetch/router change accidentally prefetches telemetry chunk on nav. The prefetch matcher includes /dashboard

evan: can confirm — Network tab shows telemetry-sidecar.js requested on initial route.
Headers:
```
GET /dashboard -> x-prefetch: true
```

miguel: oh — that's our route-affinity prefetch. It uses policy 'eager-any' which fetches all dynamic imports for first route

zoe: so two vectors: a) bundle grew b) prefetch pulled it on LCP path

sara: quick mitigation: revert the telemetry import in console-app entry and revert canary? or change prefetch policy to exclude telemetry

aleks: reverting is safest short-term. But we can also patch router to skip prefetch for chunks > 200KB. quick patch in PR 4321 proposes skipLargeChunks boolean

evan: patch looks small, but we need test across EU canary first. Suggest: revert canary now, open hotfix to change prefetch policy, and follow-up with telemetry lazy-split

zoe: agree. Opening rollback ticket.

deploy-bot: canary deployment 2026-03-21T15:23:10Z -> rolled back by @zoe

sara: created PR 4321: "router: skip prefetch for heavy chunks" — includes metric flag and unit test. Link: https://git.redwood/console/pull/4321 :hammer_and_wrench:

miguel: after that we'll add an invariant in build pipeline to warn if telemetry chunk > 150KB

aleks: longer term: move telemetry to a worker and async init so UI path doesn't touch it. I have a spike branch: `telemetry/async-worker-split`

zoe: ok team — rollback + PR + pipeline guard. I'll send a short postmortem to eng-platform and product. :eyes:

sara: thumbs up. I'll monitor perf dashboards for EU after rollback.
